prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; Switching Window Acknowledgment confirms window available), Main Transformer (abnormal trends escalated; work scheduled after loading/isolation review), export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher if capability<target; Dispatcher sets permitted export; relay applies ceiling, keeps protection unless authorized plan, stays available). Grid, port out of scope. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms→Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace→Substation Operator), Helideck. Modes: Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint, Weather Hold, Vessel Standby. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Alarms safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; operational data→Shore Control Room, keeps source timestamps; Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; routine message hub shore↔offshore; holds last validated limit on grid comms loss; incident log), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale), Operations Radio Console (voice to CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft in coverage), Personnel Tracking Console. Weather Service, Metocean Buoy inputs reviewed with offshore observations. Weather Analyst: forecast uncertainty; Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note→Duty Planner. Marine Coordinator: Berth Slot Confirmation; marine/weather info→vessels, Duty Planner; checks vessel timing vs window. Vessel Master: read-back of safety instructions; Transfer Manifest Addendum; Crew Count Correction→Personnel Tracking Console; proceed/hold. Recovery Basket Load Sheet→Rescue Coordinator. Inventory: Warehouse System authoritative; Storekeeper reconciles; substitutions need engineering acceptance. Isolation: lock/tag, absence-of-voltage test; Work Permit Portal current revision only, updated with window timing/boundaries before work; handover checks; Control Engineer verifies restoration. Switching windows: export capacity assessed first; Duty Planner consolidates, records actual times; Grid Dispatcher confirms; Grid Constraint may

New part:
S768: The Control Engineer reviews alarms and operating trends with the SCADA Engineer when an abnormal condition may require intervention.
S769: The Grid Dispatcher communicates external operating requirements to the Grid Interface Relay and the responsible control personnel.
S770: Instructions that affect electrical safety are communicated through authorized channels and confirmed by the responsible Substation Operator or Electrical Technician.
S771: When a communication channel is unavailable, personnel use the approved fallback method and report the outage as soon as practicable.
S772: Urgent messages identify the affected asset, the hazard or condition, the required action, and the person issuing the instruction.
S773: The receiver repeats critical details, and the sender confirms that the read-back is accurate before the instruction is treated as understood.
S774: Operational records identify the originator, recipient, event time, recording time, relevant asset, and decision or action taken.
S775: Entries distinguish observed facts from estimates, assumptions, and recommendations so that later reviewers can assess their basis.
S776: Records use synchronized time sources where available, and any known clock discrepancy is noted for later reconciliation.
S777: Corrections preserve the original entry, identify the person making the change, and state the reason for the correction.
S778: The Field Supervisor ensures that field observations and work outcomes are entered promptly while the details remain verifiable.
S779: The Duty Planner links relevant communications and work records to the applicable work package and operating plan.
S780: The Work Permit Portal retains permit decisions and associated approvals in a form that can be retrieved for review.
S781: The Cybersecurity Analyst protects access logs and communication records against unauthorized alteration or disclosure.
S782: The organization retains voice recordings, system logs, and work records according to the approved retention schedule and applicable legal obligations.
S783: Records subject to an investigation, claim, or safety review are preserved from routine deletion until the authorized release of the hold.
S784: The responsible manager reviews record completeness after significant events and assigns correction or follow-up actions where evidence is missing.
S785: Fire protection is designed to detect smoke, heat, and flame early enough to support automatic equipment protection and a controlled personnel response.
S786: The Fire Detection Panel supervises detection circuits and annunciates alarms with location and fault information.
S787: Detection coverage includes electrical enclosures, machinery spaces, and other areas identified by the site fire risk assessment.
S788: The Turbine Sensor Bus carries equipment status used by protective functions and operational monitoring.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
